notes: The single the of the fourth part of a hin goes to the present article morpheme on הִין, fronted because the rectum is rendered anarthrously (rule 29).

The italic of an ephah is kept inside עִשָּׂרוֹן's unit under rule 31: that noun denotes a tenth of an ephah, so the numeral's own rendering is not already complete at a tenth part. Reading the italics as rule 33's supplied head noun plus function word, and so `added`, was the competing analysis.
